plan.contextChunk: This figure is a tall two-column diagram tracing data through the two branches of a CLIP model up into a shared space. Each branch is a bottom-to-top stack of five dark-outlined parallelograms, each carrying a faint square grid and standing for one two-dimensional embedding slice. A vertical rule on the far left is labeled "Image encoder" and one on the far right is labeled "Text encoder." Between consecutive planes on the left, heavy black upward arrows pass four rounded boxes reading "ViT block x3"; the mirroring positions on the right carry four boxes reading "transformer block x3." On the left-hand planes the data appear as small colored markers whose shape and hue echo the depicted object: pink and blue squares, pink, purple, orange and blue circles, blue and purple triangles, and a green square, each joined to its position on the plane above by a thin dashed colored line. On the right-hand planes the same items appear instead as text strings such as "red circle," "green square," "purple triangle" and "blue triangle," linked across layers by dashed gray lines. At the top, a black arrow rises from each branch’s final plane into a filled orange disk beneath the heading "Joint embedding space." Following one colored marker upward alongside its text counterpart lets the reader watch the two modalities’ layouts drift toward a common arrangement layer by layer.

elements: left vertical rule labeled 'Image encoder' (rotated text) on far left
right vertical rule labeled 'Text encoder' (rotated text) on far right
five horizontal grid planes (image branch) stacked bottom-to-top at X≈-3.2, each a thin dark-outlined square with a faint 2x2 inner grid
five horizontal grid planes (text branch) stacked bottom-to-top at X≈+3.2, same style
four heavy black upward arrows between consecutive image planes, each passing a rounded box reading 'ViT block x3'
four heavy black upward arrows between consecutive text planes, each passing a rounded box reading 'transformer block x3'
colored markers on each image plane: red circle, green square, purple triangle, blue triangle, pink square, blue circle, purple circle, orange circle, pink circle (shape+hue echo the object)
thin dashed colored lines joining each image marker to its position on the plane above (per-concept trajectory)
text-string labels on each text plane ('red circle','green square','purple triangle','blue triangle','pink square','blue circle','purple circle','orange circle','pink circle')
thin dashed gray lines joining each text label to its position on the plane above (per-concept trajectory)
filled orange disk at top center beneath heading 'Joint embedding space'
black arrow rising from the top image plane into the orange disk
black arrow rising from the top text plane into the orange disk
heading text 'Joint embedding space' above the disk

interactions.label: CLIP layer
interactions.teaches: Stepping upward advances the highlighted markers and labels one stack level at a time, revealing how each encoder gradually reorganizes its layout so the two modalities converge toward a common arrangement near the joint space

Hovering one shape or text label brightens that single concept's dashed trajectory through both branches from input to top layer, making the cross-modal alignment of one idea visible while the rest stays dim

interactions.label: Branches
interactions.teaches: Isolating one branch shows the within-modality reorganization alone; showing both reveals that the meaningful image-text comparison happens only when the two layouts are brought together in the joint embedding space

demo_steps.title: Input layouts differ
demo_steps.narration: At L0 the colored markers (image) and the text labels (text) sit in quite different arrangements on their planes — the two modalities do not yet agree.

demo_steps.title: Mid-network drift
demo_steps.narration: By L2 both stacks have shifted; corresponding concepts begin to occupy similar relative positions, showing the encoders aligning their geometry.

demo_steps.title: Converged at the top
demo_steps.narration: At L4 the image markers and text labels share nearly the same layout, ready to be projected into the single orange joint-embedding disk.

demo_steps.title: One modality alone
demo_steps.narration: Switching to Image only fades the text branch, clarifying that the visible reorganization within the image encoder is independent of the text side until the joint space.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World layout: image branch centered at X=-3.2, text branch at X=+3.2. Five planes per branch at heights Y = 0, 1.6, 3.2, 4.8, 6.4; each plane is a horizontal 2.4 x 2.4 unit square in the XZ plane (thin dark outline #333, faint inner grid #cccccc). Markers ~0.12 unit sprites/shapes sitting just above each plane (Y+0.05). Orange disk: SphereGeometry/Circle ~0.7 radius at (0, 8.0, 0), fill #f4a07a with black rim; heading above it. Vertical side rules at X≈-5.2 and +5.2 spanning Y 0..7. Rounded block boxes ~1.4 x 0.4 between planes. Per-concept aligned target (u,v) in plane-local [-1,1] shared by BOTH branches at L4: red circle (-0.6,0.5), green square (0.6,0.6), purple triangle (-0.5,-0.5), blue triangle (0.7,-0.4), pink square (0.1,0.7), blue circle (-0.2,0.1), purple circle (-0.7,0.0), orange circle (0.3,0.0), pink circle (0.0,-0.6). For layer t in 0..4 use position = lerp(branchScatter, alignedTarget, t/4) where branchScatter is a seeded per-branch, per-concept offset (image scatter != text scatter) so L0 layouts differ and L4 layouts match. Colors: red #e04040, green #4caf6e, purple #9b59b6, blue #4aa3df, pink #f48fb1, orange #f0a050. Dashed image trajectories use the concept color; dashed text trajectories use gray #888. Active layer (layerStep) markers/labels at full opacity + slight scale-up, other layers ~0.35 opacity. Hovered concept's full trajectory (both branches) at opacity 1 and thicker; non-hovered dimmed.
interactionPlan.notes: Build planes as LineLoop/LineSegments grids in the XZ plane. Render markers as small instanced meshes (circle=sphere/cylinder, square=box, triangle=cone) tinted per concept; text labels as canvas-texture sprites on the right branch. Trajectories as dashed THREE.Line (LineDashedMaterial, computeLineDistances) rebuilt when layer emphasis changes. On layerStep change, animate marker/label opacity and scale per layer index. On hover, raycast markers and text sprites, map to concept id, and set per-line opacity. On branchToggle, fade the whole left or right group (planes+markers+arrows+boxes+rule) via group opacity/visibility. Keep both branches' geometry alive and toggle visibility rather than rebuilding.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Button for stepping upward through CLIP layers; the active image-plane markers and text labels advance one stack level at a time toward the joint embedding disk, showing how the two encoders gradually reorganize their layouts.
- Hover over a shape or text label to highlight its matching trajectory in both branches; the selected dashed paths brighten from input to top layer, making cross-modal alignment visible for one concept at a time.

authoredContext:
The figure shows how a
trained CLIP model maps data to embeddings. This figure is generated in
the same way as the figure: for each encoder we
reduce dimensionality for visualization using t-distributed Stochastic
Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE). For the image encoder, we show
the visual content using icons to reflect the color and shape depicted
in the image (we previously used the same visualization in the section).

CLIP mapping diagram, using the same technique as described in the section. To reduce dimensionality we apply t-SNE separately for the text encoder and the image encoder. Within each encoder, we run t-SNE jointly across all shown layers.

attempts.html: ⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: Default layer emphasis (L0) dims markers on the four upper image planes to ~0.35 opacity, so they look nearly empty versus the source where every plane shows clearly visible colored markers
Text concept labels on the right (text encoder) branch are tiny and heavily overlapping each other, unlike the legible per-concept labels in the source

Side-rule labels 'Image encoder' / 'Text encoder' are horizontal sprites that collide with the ViT/transformer block boxes, whereas the source draws them as rotated vertical text along the outer vertical rules
The orange 'Joint embedding space' disk renders as a tilted ellipse under the isometric camera instead of the front-facing circle in the source
Image-branch colored dashed trajectories are very faint (low opacity) compared to the prominent dashed colored lines in the source
evaluation.notes: All major structural elements (two 5-plane encoder columns, block boxes, arrows, side rules, orange joint-embedding disk, heading, trajectories) are present with a matching isometric-diamond composition and strong, pedagogically meaningful layer/branch/hover interactions, but the default view looks sparser than the source because non-active layers are dimmed, the text-branch labels are too small and overlapping, and the side labels are mis-oriented.
action_items: Increase the canvas font size and add vertical/horizontal jitter or leader offsets for the text-branch concept sprites so they do not overlap and are comfortably readable
Render the 'Image encoder' / 'Text encoder' side labels as rotated vertical text placed outside the block boxes to match the source layout
Raise the baseline opacity of markers and trajectories on non-active layers (or initialize at the top layer) so the default screenshot shows populated planes like the source
Billboard the orange disk (and its rim) to face the camera so it appears as a circle rather than a tilted ellipse

feedback.rationale: Concept and interactivity are strong (both 5/5) with no plan action items; all four action items are concrete implementation fixes (label sizing/spacing, side-label orientation, default opacity, disk billboarding) that the generator can address without changing the plan.

attempts.html: ⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: Source is a flat front-on 2D schematic, but the generated figure uses a 30/30 axonometric tilt that turns the plane stacks into a tilted 3D pile, hurting recognizability and causing heavy element overlap
Text-branch concept labels ('red circle', 'purple triangle', etc.) are densely overlapping and illegible at every layer, unlike the source where they are spread around each plane
The 'ViT block x3' boxes and the vertical 'Image encoder' side-rule text overlap the left plane stack instead of sitting cleanly to the side as in the source
The whole composition is small and pushed into the left-center with large empty regions, whereas the source fills the frame with two tall, well-separated columns
Marker/trajectory colors and shapes are roughly correct, but the tilted view makes the dashed trajectories and per-layer scatter hard to read compared to the clean vertical convergence in the source

plan.contextChunk: This figure is a tall two-column diagram tracing data through the two branches of a CLIP model up into a shared space. Each branch is a bottom-to-top stack of five dark-outlined parallelograms, each carrying a faint square grid and standing for one two-dimensional embedding slice. A vertical rule on the far left is labeled "Image encoder" and one on the far right is labeled "Text encoder." Between consecutive planes on the left, heavy black upward arrows pass four rounded boxes reading "ViT block x3"; the mirroring positions on the right carry four boxes reading "transformer block x3." On the left-hand planes the data appear as small colored markers whose shape and hue echo the depicted object: pink and blue squares, pink, purple, orange and blue circles, blue and purple triangles, and a green square, each joined to its position on the plane above by a thin dashed colored line. On the right-hand planes the same items appear instead as text strings such as "red circle," "green square," "purple triangle" and "blue triangle," linked across layers by dashed gray lines. At the top, a black arrow rises from each branch’s final plane into a filled orange disk beneath the heading "Joint embedding space." Following one colored marker upward alongside its text counterpart lets the reader watch the two modalities’ layouts drift toward a common arrangement layer by layer.

interactions.label: CLIP layer
interactions.teaches: Stepping upward advances the highlighted markers and labels one stack level at a time, revealing how each encoder gradually reorganizes its layout so the two modalities converge toward a common arrangement near the joint space

Hovering one shape or text label brightens that single concept's dashed trajectory through both branches from input to top layer, making the cross-modal alignment of one idea visible while the rest stays dim

interactions.label: Branches
interactions.teaches: Isolating one branch shows the within-modality reorganization alone; showing both reveals that the meaningful image-text comparison happens only when the two layouts are brought together in the joint embedding space

demo_steps.title: Input layouts differ
demo_steps.narration: At L0 the colored markers (image) and the text labels (text) sit in quite different arrangements on their planes — the two modalities do not yet agree.

demo_steps.title: Mid-network drift
demo_steps.narration: By L2 both stacks have shifted; corresponding concepts begin to occupy similar relative positions, showing the encoders aligning their geometry.

demo_steps.title: Converged at the top
demo_steps.narration: At L4 the image markers and text labels share nearly the same layout, ready to be projected into the single orange joint-embedding disk.

demo_steps.title: One modality alone
demo_steps.narration: Switching to Image only fades the text branch, clarifying that the visible reorganization within the image encoder is independent of the text side until the joint space.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World layout: image branch centered at X=-3.2, text branch at X=+3.2. Five planes per branch at heights Y = 0, 1.6, 3.2, 4.8, 6.4; each plane is a horizontal 2.4 x 2.4 unit square in the XZ plane (thin dark outline #333, faint inner grid #cccccc). Markers ~0.12 unit sprites/shapes sitting just above each plane (Y+0.05). Orange disk: SphereGeometry/Circle ~0.7 radius at (0, 8.0, 0), fill #f4a07a with black rim; heading above it. Vertical side rules at X≈-5.2 and +5.2 spanning Y 0..7. Rounded block boxes ~1.4 x 0.4 between planes. Per-concept aligned target (u,v) in plane-local [-1,1] shared by BOTH branches at L4: red circle (-0.6,0.5), green square (0.6,0.6), purple triangle (-0.5,-0.5), blue triangle (0.7,-0.4), pink square (0.1,0.7), blue circle (-0.2,0.1), purple circle (-0.7,0.0), orange circle (0.3,0.0), pink circle (0.0,-0.6). For layer t in 0..4 use position = lerp(branchScatter, alignedTarget, t/4) where branchScatter is a seeded per-branch, per-concept offset (image scatter != text scatter) so L0 layouts differ and L4 layouts match. Colors: red #e04040, green #4caf6e, purple #9b59b6, blue #4aa3df, pink #f48fb1, orange #f0a050. Dashed image trajectories use the concept color; dashed text trajectories use gray #888. Active layer (layerStep) markers/labels at full opacity + slight scale-up, other layers ~0.35 opacity. Hovered concept's full trajectory (both branches) at opacity 1 and thicker; non-hovered dimmed.
interactionPlan.notes: Build planes as LineLoop/LineSegments grids in the XZ plane. Render markers as small instanced meshes (circle=sphere/cylinder, square=box, triangle=cone) tinted per concept; text labels as canvas-texture sprites on the right branch. Trajectories as dashed THREE.Line (LineDashedMaterial, computeLineDistances) rebuilt when layer emphasis changes. On layerStep change, animate marker/label opacity and scale per layer index. On hover, raycast markers and text sprites, map to concept id, and set per-line opacity. On branchToggle, fade the whole left or right group (planes+markers+arrows+boxes+rule) via group opacity/visibility. Keep both branches' geometry alive and toggle visibility rather than rebuilding.
